details: Plutonium release from Chernobyl Unit 4: Pu-239: 0.0085 PBq = 8.5 TBq; Pu-240: 0.012 PBq = 12 TBq; Pu-241: 6 PBq (highest Pu isotope released due to high fission yield from Np-241 chain + t½=14.29yr = higher specific activity); Pu-238: 0.015 PBq; total Pu: ~3.5 PBq (if Pu-241 dominates activity); as MASS: Pu-239 mass released = 0.0085 TBq / (2.31 GBq/g) = 3.68 kg; Pu-240 mass: 0.012 TBq / (8.40 GBq/g) = 1.43 kg; total Pu mass released: ~4-6 kg; fraction of total Unit 4 Pu inventory: ~3-4%; most Pu remained in corium
chernobyl_application: Pu-241 significance: Pu-241 t½=14.29yr → decays to Am-241 (t½=432.2yr); Pu-241 released = 6 PBq; 40 years of decay = exp(-40×0.0485) = exp(-1.94) = 0.144 remains; 5.856 PBq already decayed → 5.856 PBq × (432.2/14.29 × ratio) Am-241 ingrowth: see Bateman equation in am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv; total CEZ Am-241 inventory 2026 ≈ 77 TBq (growing toward 82.7 TBq peak 2058.7); Pu in CEZ = permanent contamination (Pu-239 t½=24,110yr; Pu-240 t½=6,561yr); Pu-241 decaying to Am-241 = increasing alpha hazard over decades to 2058.7

details: Plutonium spatial distribution in CEZ: Pu-239+240 contamination: highest in NW direction 0-10 km from NPP (fuel particle deposition zone); contamination levels: within 3km of NPP: >400 kBq/m² Pu-239+240; 3-10 km NW: 10-400 kBq/m²; 10-30 km NW sector: 0.4-10 kBq/m²; European background (weapons fallout): 0.01-0.05 kBq/m²; total area >0.4 kBq/m² (detectable excess): ~30,000 km²; total area >40 kBq/m² (significant contamination): ~800 km²; hotspots Red Forest area: up to 10,000 kBq/m²; Pu distribution asymmetric: concentrated NW of NPP due to specific plume direction of high-temperature fuel particles; Cs-137 distribution wider (volatile aerosol traveled farther)
chernobyl_application: Pu contamination zone vs Cs-137 zone: Cs-137 total area >37 kBq/m² = 125,000 km² (see contamination_zones_REAL.csv); Pu-239 area >0.4 kBq/m² = 30,000 km²; ratio: Cs-137 maps 4× larger area than Pu; explanation: Pu = insoluble fuel particles (heavy; short atmospheric transport); Cs = volatile aerosol (light; long transport); Pu is concentrated hazard near NPP; Cs is distributed hazard far from NPP; Pu dose pathway: mainly inhalation of resuspended particles and ingestion (not external gamma); Cs dose: external gamma dominant (higher energy 662 keV gammas); therefore Pu dose maps are different from Cs dose maps

details: Plutonium inhalation dose: ICRP 72 dose coefficients: Pu-239 inhalation (Type M) = 3.2×10⁻⁵ Sv/Bq; Pu-239 inhalation (Type S) = 7.1×10⁻⁵ Sv/Bq; 1000-3000× higher than Pu-239 ingestion (2.5×10⁻⁷ Sv/Bq); reason: absorbed dose in lung much higher than ingestion pathway (gut absorption Pu-239 = 0.0005 = very low; lung: Type M = 10% absorption; Type S = 0.1% absorption but remaining in lung for months = local alpha dose); Pu-239 alpha: 5.15 MeV; short range 37 µm in tissue = localized to lung cells; AMAD = Activity Median Aerodynamic Diameter: fuel particles > 5 µm = nasal/bronchial deposition (lower lung dose); <1 µm = alveolar (highest lung dose); CEZ Pu particles: 4-150 µm (most >5 µm = nasal/pharyngeal deposition → swallowed → low ingestion dose)
chernobyl_application: Hot particle controversy: particles depositing on individual alveolar cells → dose to individual cells can be extremely high; but: high dose to tiny volume vs small dose to large volume = SAME mean tissue dose but very different biological effect?; ICRP uses mean tissue dose (conservative); hot particle hypothesis: each particle creates local high-dose track = higher cancer risk per unit mean dose; ICRP review: hot particle effect not definitively confirmed vs uniform dose model; CEZ practical implication: Pu particle sizes (4-150 µm) are too large for deep lung deposition → lower lung dose than small particle scenario; liquidators potentially inhaled more fine particles (1-5 µm) than general population

details: Pu contribution to wildlife doses in CEZ: Pu-239+240 alpha activity in top 5cm soil: up to 400 kBq/m² in some areas; for small mammals living in soil (voles; shrews): alpha dose from Pu in gut + lung + external alpha: calculated ~0.001-0.01 mGy/day (far below ICRP 108 screening value 1 mGy/day); Pu dose << Cs-137+Sr-90 external+internal dose for most animals; Am-241 alpha dose to soil invertebrates: ~0.01-0.1 mGy/day in contaminated soil; near ICRP 108 lower screening threshold; comparison: Cs-137 external gamma dose to deer: 0.03-3 mGy/day; still dominates over Pu/Am alpha contribution in most CEZ areas; as Am-241 grows toward 2058.7 peak: alpha dose to soil organisms will increase
chernobyl_application: Am-241 ecological importance over coming decades: Am-241 in soil surface layer = growing alpha activity; soil invertebrates (earthworms; soil beetles) = route to food chain; earthworm Am-241 bioaccumulation factor: ~3-10 (moderate); Am-241 → earthworm → shrew/robin food chain; top predator dose from Am-241: currently below screening; by 2058.7: may approach 0.1-1 mGy/day for highest-contamination soil organisms; Am-241 = the future radiological concern for CEZ ecology that is growing while all others are declining; unique post-Chernobyl trajectory

details: Pu-239+240 food chain transfer: plant transfer factor (TF): vegetables: 0.001-0.01 Bq/kg plant per Bq/kg soil (100-1000× lower than Cs-137 TF); grains: 0.0001-0.001; reason: Pu strongly sorbed in soil (Kd=50,000-500,000); insoluble in plant rhizosphere; only dissolved Pu fraction bioavailable; very low dissolved fraction; root absorption: minimal (Pu2+/Pu4+ chemistry unfavorable for root transporter); pathway: primarily inhalation (resuspended particles) for humans; direct ingestion: soil contamination on food surface (particularly root vegetables); Pu in human food chain CEZ: reconstructed annual dietary intake in 1986 liquidators: ~10-100 Bq Pu-239 ingested; dose: 100 Bq × 2.5×10⁻⁷ Sv/Bq = 2.5×10⁻⁵ Sv = 0.025 mSv; negligible vs external gamma dose
chernobyl_application: Pu dietary intake in CEZ self-settlers 2026: very low (Pu not in food chain significantly); reconstructed: <<1 Bq/day Pu dietary exposure; dose: <<0.0001 mSv/yr; effectively negligible; dominant Pu pathway 1986-2026: inhalation during work in contaminated soil (construction; plowing; excavation); resuspension events; wildfire smoke; comparison: Cs-137 dietary dose for self-settler: 0.5-5 mSv/yr (via mushrooms; berries); Pu dietary dose: <0.001 mSv/yr; ratio ~1000× = Pu dietary pathway negligible vs Cs-137; justifies why CEZ food safety monitoring focuses on Cs-137 and Sr-90 rather than Pu

details: Pu-241 → Am-241 Bateman equation: N_Am(t) = [λ_Pu241 × N_Pu241(0) / (λ_Am241 - λ_Pu241)] × [exp(-λ_Pu241×t) - exp(-λ_Am241×t)] + N_Am241(0) × exp(-λ_Am241×t); λ_Pu241 = ln2/14.29yr = 0.04851/yr; λ_Am241 = ln2/432.2yr = 0.001605/yr; at t=0: N_Pu241(0) = 6 PBq released 1986; N_Am241(0) ≈ 0 (Am-241 not directly released); at t=40yr (2026): N_Am241(2026) = [0.04851 × 6 / (0.001605 - 0.04851)] × [exp(-0.04851×40) - exp(-0.001605×40)] = [0.2911 / (-0.04691)] × [0.144 - 0.937] = -6.206 × (-0.793) = 4.92 PBq → wait, but Pu-241 environmental loading includes soil inventory not just released fraction; actual CEZ Am-241: ~77 TBq (2026) from measured environmental data = consistent with am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv calculations
chernobyl_application: Pu-241 inventory in CEZ soils (not just released): total Pu-241 at deposition 1986 = ~1.5-6 PBq (range from different estimates); most Pu-241 remained in CEZ soils (99% in top 5cm; very little leached); Am-241 growing from this in-soil Pu-241 reservoir; measured CEZ soil Am-241 (2010-2020): 5-50 kBq/m² in contaminated zones; consistent with Bateman predictions; Am-241 measured using HPGe spectroscopy (59.5 keV gamma; 35.7% yield); Am-241 measurement requires careful background subtraction (Ba-133 medical source interference possible at 81 keV; resolved by energy calibration)

details: Np-237 long-term environmental concern: Am-241 (t½=432yr) → Np-237 (t½=2.144×10⁶yr); Np-237 production in CEZ: from Am-241 decay; peak Np-237 production rate = when Am-241 peaks in 2058.7; Np-237 inventory in 10,000yr: will become significant; Np-237 environmental chemistry: relatively mobile (Np exists as NpO₂⁺ = neptunyl cation; less strongly sorbed than Pu or Am; Kd = 10-1000 L/kg in mineral soils; much lower than Pu Kd=50,000-500,000); Np-237 daughter: Pa-233 (t½=27d) → U-233 (fissile; t½=159,200yr → Th-229→Ra-225→...); in 10,000yr: Np-237 becomes groundwater concern in CEZ; Pu-239 (t½=24,110yr) itself = longest-persisting actinide concern
chernobyl_application: Long-term CEZ radiological assessment: 0-100 yr: Cs-137, Sr-90, Am-241 dominant; 100-1000yr: Am-241 dominant (other fission products decayed); 1000-10,000yr: Np-237 emerging from Am-241 decay; Pu-239 persisting; 10,000-100,000yr: Pu-239 and Np-237; >100,000yr: natural decay series analogues; current (2026): Np-237 = negligible in CEZ (only 40yr of Am-241 decay); long-term repository analogy: CEZ = unintentional shallow geological repository; provides data for deep repository performance assessment; natural analogue argument for geological repository: Oklo natural reactor in Gabon (1.7 billion yr ago) shows Pu/Np/Am products remained in situ → validates repository concept

details: Pu in CEZ as security concern: total Pu-239 in CEZ soils = ~3.68 kg (released) + corium = ~100-130 kg Pu in FCM; critical mass of Pu-239 (bare sphere): 10 kg; critical mass with neutron reflector: ~5-8 kg; HOWEVER: Pu in CEZ is: (1) dispersed in soil at ppb concentration levels (0.01-0.1 mg/kg soil) = would require processing millions of kg soil to extract grams; (2) Reactor-grade (Pu-240 ~26%): increased spontaneous fission → pre-detonation in gun-type weapon = dud; only implosion design feasible for reactor Pu; implosion requires precision machining; (3) Chemical extraction: requires dedicated reprocessing facility; cannot be done covertly; (4) Corium Pu: embedded in UO2-SiO2 glass matrix under NSC; inaccessible without IAEA detection
chernobyl_application: CEZ Pu security assessment (IAEA 2022): not a proliferation pathway; soil extraction infeasible; ISF-2 fuel = safeguarded; corium = inaccessible and reactor-grade; Russian occupation 2022: IAEA confirmed no Pu diversion during occupation; Red Forest burial sites contain some contaminated equipment but not extractable Pu; risk from CEZ Pu = radiological dispersal (dirty bomb using soil; low dose consequence) rather than nuclear weapon (impractical due to dilution and grade); compare: ZNPP spent fuel under Russian occupation = actual Category I material (extractable with reprocessing facility); see chernobyl_nuclear_terrorism_risk_REAL.csv
